faq.q: Which exam and ID presets are built in?
faq.a: One-click presets set the pixel size, the upper size limit and the lower limit: SSC Photo 200×230 (20–50 KB) and Signature 140×60 (10–20 KB, the 4.0 × 2.0 cm size); UPSC Photo 350×350 (20–200 KB; UPSC sets the file size and face coverage, not a pixel size, so a square 350×350 is used) and Signature 500×350 (20–100 KB, the 350–500 pixel range in the 2026 UPSC guidelines); IBPS Photo 200×230 (20–50 KB) and Signature 140×60 (10–20 KB); Passport Photo (600×800) and Aadhaar Photo (400×400), plus size-only presets for under 100 KB, 50 KB and 20 KB. Photos are centre-cropped to the box; signatures are fitted whole on white so nothing is cut. If the result is below the lower limit you get a warning. Notices change between recruitments, so check the one you are applying for.

faq.q: How does it hit an exact target file size in KB?
faq.a: Enter a Target Size (KB) and the compressor runs a binary search of about 8 iterations on the JPEG/WebP quality to find the largest quality that stays under your limit. If it can't reach the target even at the lowest quality, the result is flagged with a 'Could not reach target' warning rather than failing silently.

faq.q: What output formats are available and what does 'Enhance Quality' do?
faq.a: Output can be JPG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF (with automatic fallback to WebP if your browser can't encode AVIF). The 'Enhance Quality' checkbox applies an unsharp-mask sharpen and a slight contrast boost before compressing — useful for old scanned photos — using a blurred copy to compute the sharpening.

faq.q: Can I compress many images at once and compare the result?
faq.a: Yes, it's batch: drop multiple files, compress them together, download each individually or all as a ZIP, with a total before/after size summary. The first image also gets a draggable before/after comparison slider. Everything runs in your browser via canvas — nothing is uploaded, and EXIF is dropped by the canvas re-encode.
